_notice: Assertions this project made and then withdrew, with the phrasing each was made in. Written because a claim lives wherever it was copied, and the ledger is not the inventory: when CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01 was reworded on 2026-07-29, the withdrawn attribution was still live in three publication surfaces the ledger has no knowledge of — README.md, the write-up draft, and a generated appendix. tests/test_withdrawn_assertions.py searches tracked prose for the PHRASING, not the claim ID, because a copy carries the words and usually drops the identifier.
_how_to_use: When a claim's wording is narrowed or withdrawn, add the retired phrasing here in the same change. Add permitted_in entries only for files that must carry the words to do their job — a historical record of what was once asserted, or a document quoting the phrase in order to report it withdrawn. An exemption whose file no longer contains the phrase fails the suite, so the list cannot rot into a blanket.

assertions.what_it_asserted: That the 87% of QLoRA residual loss sitting in the content-bearing channel was output naming the wrong entity — an error-category attribution.
assertions.why_withdrawn: The loss decomposition measures WHERE loss sits, not which error category produced it. The attribution's only source was ADR 0007's unquantified inspection of two development examples, which the accepted plan's section 12.3 forbids generalising from. A measurement points the other way: false positives exceed false negatives by 637 arguments on those frames, which is over-generation rather than entity-naming. Raised as finding O2 by the review that refused to close Plan 3.

assertions._found_by_the_check_itself: The two entries above were NOT in the first version of this list. The author enumerated five permitted files by hand and the check found two more on its first run — one of them a file the author had regenerated minutes earlier. That is the lesson this register exists for, arriving immediately: an inventory assembled by memory is short, and only a search over the corpus is an inventory.
assertions._the_paraphrase_this_check_could_not_cat: The literal-match limit is not hypothetical and it cost something. TWO surfaces carried the same attribution in paraphrase and passed this check clean: docs/plan3/certification-result.md said the 87% was 'the coreference and entity-selection errors ADR 0007 catalogued' — a STRONGER form, naming two section 12.1 categories, on the primary result document that six ledger claims cite — and docs/plan3/HANDOFF-2026-07-22-reanalysis.md said 'grounded, well-formed, wrong-entity'. Both were found by an independent reviewer on 2026-07-29, not by this test. Their phrasings are now registered below so the literal check covers them, but the general lesson stands and is recorded in REVIEW.md: a paraphrase defeats a phrase search, so reconciling a reworded claim against its copies remains a reader's job.

assertions.what_it_asserted: That grounding fidelity and certifiability are ORTHOGONAL - i.e. independent - for grounded event-argument extraction on RAMS.
assertions.why_withdrawn: Orthogonality asserts independence. One intervention observed across three systems cannot establish it and ADR 0011 did not test it; at group level the two are in fact weakly associated (Spearman rho = -0.206, p ~ 8e-15) while the 1,266 fully-grounded QA groups still average 0.589 loss. The measured relation is a DISSOCIATION. Registered LATE: the narrowing landed in commit d256ca5 and this file's own rule requires registration in the same change; an independent review caught the omission (finding F2, 2026-08-02).
assertions._why_this_phrase_and_not_the_bare_word: The bare word 'orthogonal' appears in about 40 files because it is inside the RETAINED claim identifier CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01, which is deliberately kept for traceability. Registering the bare word would flag every legitimate mention of the identifier and would train readers to ignore this check. The phrase registered here is the assertion, not the word.
assertions._the_shorthand_this_phrase_does_not_catc: The symbol forms 'grounding perp certifiability' and 'grounding perp certifiability' (spaced and unspaced) are the same assertion in shorthand and are NOT matched by a literal search for this phrase. They were located by hand on 2026-08-02 and dealt with individually: ADR 0011 line 189 reworded with a pointer to Amendment 1, docs/plan3/HANDOFF-2026-07-22-reanalysis.md given a superseded-wording banner, and docs/plan4/accepted-plan.md left untouched as a frozen hash-pinned accepted plan. This is the literal-match limit this register already records, recurring.

assertions.phrase: capability gap rather than a limitation of the certification method
assertions.what_it_asserted: That the whole infeasibility was a property of the model and score, and that the certification method contributed nothing to it.
assertions.why_withdrawn: The claim covered two causes and attributed both to capability. Only the first is that: the score reaches 2.0% where a perfect ranking of the same population reaches 23.6%, and that gap is the score's. The second is the finite-sample penalty, which is a property of the corpus and the delta allocation and not of any model - at n = 1,396 with delta/3 the certifier's Hoeffding bound spends 0.0925 of the 0.20 risk budget before any data is seen, so a certificate at the acceptance floor needs an accepted set carrying mean loss at most 0.1075 whoever produced it. Calling that a capability gap ran in the flattering direction and folded a benchmark finding into a task finding, so the project reported one result where it had two. Owner ruling, 2026-08-03.

assertions.what_it_asserted: That the abstain/extract flip rate between serving stacks lies in an interval from 1.3% to 1.8%, which reads as sampling uncertainty around one measurement.
assertions.why_withdrawn: IT IS NOT AN INTERVAL AND BOTH ENDPOINTS ARE CORRECT. 1.33% is the flip rate at full acceptance (4 of 300) and 1.78% is the SAME FOUR FLIPS over the top-75% denominator (4 of 225) - one numerator, two denominators, two measurements of different things. Dash-joining them asserts a sampling uncertainty neither figure carries. This is a COMPOSITION defect: no value check and no configuration check could see it, because every value involved is right and only the form is wrong. Its sibling is the withdrawn 12.9x, where a presentational choice ran the other way and manufactured a quantity that was correct nowhere.
assertions.registry_limitation_this_entry_exposes: This register matches LITERAL PHRASES, so it can catch this exact string recurring and cannot express the CLASS - 'two measurements over different denominators printed as a range'. A value-keyed register has no way to say 'these numbers are individually correct and their composition is not'. Recorded as a finding about the register rather than worked around: the entry below is a tripwire for one instance, not coverage of a class, and nothing automated fills that gap.
